data.name: Mustatab
data.gender_notes: Mustatab is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'stb' meaning to strive or yearn. In Islamic context, it refers to someone who is eagerly seeking Allah's pleasure and reward in the hereafter. The name Mustatab carries the meaning “Seeking or yearning” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mustatab usually hope their child will grow to embody seeking or yearning and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Striving towards Allah's pleasure and seeking His blessings.
data.etymology: Mustatab belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Seeking or yearning.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mustatab total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

historical_references.time_period: During the caliphate of Umar ibn Abdulaziz (Umar II) (683-693 AD)
historical_references.context: Mustatab ibn Abi-Sharik was a companion of Abu Hurairah who narrated Hadith. When Umar II came to power, Mustatab was given the position of treasurer. However, he was accused of embezzlement and Umar II ordered him to return the stolen wealth. Mustatab denied the accusation and invited Umar II to his house. When Umar II entered the house, he found the stolen wealth there. Mustatab confessed and was immediately executed.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Barr's Al-Isti'ab, Volume 3, Page 1307. The name Mustatab carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mustatab ibn Jabalah was an Arab poet and scholar from the Banu Tamim tribe. He is known for his poetry and his work in the field of Islamic jurisprudence. He was a student of Imam Malik and is considered an important figure in the development of the Islamic legal tradition. Mustatab is also known for his role in the dissemination of Hadith and his support for the early caliphs.
